successors.name: Kingdom of Tonga
successors.text: the Tongan islands: Tongatapu, ʻEua, Haʻapai, Vavaʻu and the Niuas

ledger.x: 950: ʻAhoʻeitu, first Tuʻi Tonga, begins to expand his rule beyond Tonga.
1100: the Tongan group under the Tuʻi Tonga.
1100: Samoa pays tribute to the Tuʻi Tonga.
1100: the eastern Fijian islands within the Tongan realm.
1100: Niue, Rotuma and Tokelau as tributaries.
1450: Tongan invasions bring ʻUvea and Futuna under the Tuʻi Tonga.
1535: the Haʻa Takalaua line takes effective rule.
1535: the outer tributaries fall away with the Tuʻi Tonga's decline.
1535: tribute from Niue, Rotuma and Tokelau lapses.
1600: the Tongan hold on ʻUvea and Futuna ends with the 16th-century invasions.
1610: the Tuʻi Kanokupolu line is created.
1799: the murder of Tukuʻaho breaks Tonga into warring chiefdoms.

wars.name: Samoan expulsion of the Tongans
wars.outcome: Tuʻi Tonga Talakaifaiki defeated by Tuna, Fata and Savea; the Tongans expelled from Samoa and the Malietoa title founded.

wars.name: Tongan civil war (from 1799)
wars.outcome: Fifty years of civil war after Tukuʻaho's murder in 1799; Tāufaʻāhau of Haʻapai (1820) takes Vavaʻu (1833) and Tongatapu (1845) and founds the Kingdom of Tonga.

certainty.note: Oral-tradition chronology throughout: the capitals' spans, the tributaries' years and the 1100 and 1250 dates are placings within the pages' centuries; only the island coasts are sharp.
